source_text: ἀρεσκούσας καὶ ἡμᾶς εὐεργετούσας· ἔπειτα καὶ ὑμῖν· καὶ τοσούτῳ «ἔπειτα», ὅσῳ πρέπει μετὰ τὴν ἄκτιστον κτιστῆς εὐπρεπῶς μνημονεύειν φύσεως τάξαντας· ἱκετεύσατε ἰδικῶς ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ καὶ τῶν ἐξ ἐμοῦ καὶ σὺν ἐμοὶ καὶ πάντων τούτου γὰρ 77 πλέον παρέχειν ἡμῖν οὐκ ἐπετράπητε, τήν τε ἐπὶ τούτῳ γνώμην διατηρηθῆναί μοι ἀκίνητον, τήν τε εὐχὴν ἐπ' ἄπειρον κατορθοῦσα ἀγαθωτάτη καὶ αὐτοτελὴς καὶ ἀδιαίρετος τρίας, προσδεχθῆναι· καὶ καταξιωθῆναι ἡμᾶς παντεκνεὶ, πανοικεὶ, παγγενεὶ καὶ παμφιλεὶ φίλοι δὲ ἡμῖν οἱ ὀρθόδοξοι σὺν ὑμῖν τε καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἁγίοις ἁγιοτρισσολογῆσαι αὐτὴν ἐν οὐρανοῖς εἰς τοὺς ἀπεράντους αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων καὶ τῆς ἐπηγγελμένης καὶ πρὸς ἡμῶν πιστευομένης ἀτελευτήτου καὶ ἀδιαιρέτου αὐτῆς βασιλείας χάριν αὐτῆς τυχεῖν. ἀμήν, ἀμήν, ἀμήν. 7.9ν ὅτι σὺν τῷ Χριστῷ κρίνειν μέλλει τὰ πάντα ἀλλ' ὥρα γὰρ εἰς τὴν ἀρχθεῖσαν ὑπόθεσιν αὖθις οὖν τείνεσθαι, ὅτι σὺν τῷ Χριστῷ, ἅτε θεὸς καὶ δημιουργός, τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα κρίνειν μέλλει τὰ πάντα. τίνος γὰρ καὶ ἔστιν κρίναι ἢ τοῦ κοινωνίαν ἔχοντος πρὸς τὸν ποιήσαντα αὐτά, θεότητος καὶ βασιλείας; ὡς προφητεύει Ἠσαῖας μέν· «ἐξελεύσεται ῥάβδος ἐκ τῆς ῥίζης Ἰεσσαὶ καὶ ἄνθος ἐκ τῆς ῥίζης ἀναβήσεται. καὶ ἀναπαύσεται ἐπ' αὐτὸν πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ, πνεῦμα σοφίας καὶ συνέσεως, πνεῦμα βουλῆς καὶ ἰσχύος, πνεῦμα γνώσεως καὶ εὐσεβείας· καὶ ἐμπλήσει αὐτὸν πνεῦμα φόβου θεοῦ. οὐ κατὰ τὴν δόξαν κρινεῖ οὐδὲ κατὰ τὴν λαλιὰν ἐλέγξει· ἀλλὰ κρινεῖ τα πεινῷ κρίσιν καὶ ἐλέγξει τοὺς ὑπερηφάνους καὶ ἐξελεῖται τοὺς ταπεινοὺς τῆς γῆς, καὶ πατάξει τὴν γῆν τῷ λόγῳ τοῦ στόματος αὐ τοῦ καὶ ἐν πνεύματι διὰ χειλέων ἀνελεῖ ἀσεβεῖς.» ῥάβδον καὶ ἄνθος ἐκ τῆς ῥίζης Ἰεσσαὶ λέγει τὸν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἐν τῇ ἐνανθρωπήσει βλαστήσαντα καὶ τῇ ἑαυτοῦ εὐωδίᾳ τὴν ὑφήλιον ῥώσαντα, ἐφ' ὃν εἴδομεν ἐν εὐαγγελίοις ἀναπαυσάμενον τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, κριτὴν δὲ αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι ἐν τῇ
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing from the previous section: ... the Trinity, which supplies thoughts and wise phrases both to it] pleasing and benefiting us; then also to you; and 'then' to the degree that it is fitting, having arranged in order, to mention becomingly the created nature after the uncreated. Beseech specially on behalf of me and of those from me and with me and of all (for you were not permitted to provide us with more than this [page number 77, debris]): that my resolve in this be kept unmoved for me, and that the prayer be accepted, [the prayer] which, most good and self-complete and undivided Trinity, you bring to success without limit; and that we be counted worthy, with all our children, all our household, all our kin and all our friends (and friends to us are the orthodox), with you and all the saints, to praise it as thrice-holy in the heavens to the boundless ages of ages, and by its grace to obtain its promised kingdom, believed by us, unending and undivided. Amen, amen, amen. 7.9ν [Chapter title:] That with Christ it is going to judge all things. But it is time then to stretch again toward the subject that was begun, that with Christ, as God and Creator, the Holy Spirit is going to judge all things. For whose is it also to judge, if not of the one having communion with the one who made them, of godhead and of kingship? As Isaiah on the one hand prophesies: 'A rod will come out from the root of Jesse and a flower will go up from the root. And the Spirit of God will rest upon him, a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and strength, a spirit of knowledge and godliness; and a spirit of the fear of God will fill him. He will not judge according to the appearance, nor will he convict according to the talk; but he will judge judgment for the lowly and will convict the arrogant and will rescue the lowly of the earth, and will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and in spirit through lips he will destroy the ungodly.' He calls 'rod and flower from the root of Jesse' the one who sprouted from it in the incarnation and strengthened the land under the sun with his own fragrance, upon whom we saw in the Gospels the Holy Spirit resting, but [him] as judge with the Holy Spirit in the [continues in the next section] ...
pass_b_english: …pleasing, and doing good to us; and then to you as well. And “then” only so far as it is fitting, when things are set in their order, to make due mention of the created nature after the uncreated. Pray especially for me, for those who come from me and those who are with me, and for all (for you have not been permitted to grant us more than this): that my resolve in this may be kept unmoved; that the prayer may be accepted, which you, most good, self-complete and undivided Trinity, bring to fulfilment without end; and that we may be counted worthy, with all our children, all our household, all our kin and all our friends (and our friends are the orthodox), together with you and all the saints, to sing the thrice-holy praise of the Trinity in the heavens to the endless ages of ages, and by its grace to obtain its kingdom, promised and believed by us, which has no end and is not divided. Amen, amen, amen.
That with Christ he will judge all things.

But it is time to turn back again to the subject we began: that the Holy Spirit, being God and Creator, will judge all things with Christ. For whose task is it to judge, if not his who shares with their Maker in godhead and kingship? So Isaiah prophesies: “A rod shall come out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up from the root. And the Spirit of God shall rest upon him, a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and strength, a spirit of knowledge and godliness; and a spirit of the fear of God shall fill him. He will not judge by appearance, nor convict by what people say; but he will give judgment to the lowly, and convict the proud, and rescue the lowly of the earth; and he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with the Spirit, through his lips, he will destroy the ungodly” (Isaiah 11:1-4).

He calls “a rod and a flower from the root of Jesse” the one who sprang from that root in the incarnation and with his own fragrance gave strength to the whole world under the sun. lemmas.gloss: praise as thrice holy, sing the thrice-holy

choices.issue: Garbled draft; clauses dropped; chapter title run into the text; Isaiah misread
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u19): retranslated. Old English rendered ἀρεσκούσας as 'Having listened to us', ἱκετεύσατε ἰδικῶς as 'Entreat privately', made the Trinity the object of 'making' in the prayer, dropped παντεκνεί, πανοικεί, παγγενεί καὶ παμφιλεί, the aside 'our friends are the orthodox' and 'with you and all the saints', ran the 7.9 chapter title into the text ('For all things are to judge with Christ'), and in Isaiah 11:4 gave 'tread' for πατάξει, 'lift up' for ἀνελεῖ, 'select' for ἐξελεῖται; ὑφήλιον became 'the hills'. Reference (Isa 11:1-4) written in full; (John 1:32) added for the Spirit resting on Christ.

choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence: the previous section ends ἐνθυμήσεις καὶ φράσεις σοφὰς αὐτῇ τε ('thoughts and wise words, both to itself'). Only the words this section holds are translated.

choices.english: And “then” only so far as it is fitting, when things are set in their order
choices.why: Didymus explains his word ἔπειτα: the archangels come second only because the created must be named after the uncreated.

choices.english: for you have not been permitted to grant us more than this
choices.why: 77 is a printed page number in the copy-text, skipped.

choices.term: τήν τε εὐχὴν ἐπ' ἄπειρον κατορθοῦσα ἀγαθωτάτη ... τρίας, προσδεχθῆναι
choices.english: that the prayer may be accepted, which you, most good, self-complete and undivided Trinity, bring to fulfilment without end
choices.why: The nominative τρίας with its participle breaks into the request as an address to the Trinity; it is turned into a relative clause so the sentence stays whole.

choices.english: to sing the thrice-holy praise of the Trinity
choices.why: A rare compound: to praise with the threefold 'Holy' (Isaiah 6:3). 'The Trinity' is written for αὐτήν so the English referent is clear; no bracket.
χάριν is read as the Trinity's grace by which the kingdom is obtained; 'for its sake' is possible. τυχεῖν governs τῆς ... βασιλείας.

choices.term: 7.9ν ὅτι σὺν τῷ Χριστῷ κρίνειν μέλλει τὰ πάντα
choices.english: That with Christ he will judge all things.
choices.why: Chapter title, given its own paragraph; the subject is the Holy Spirit, as the next sentence says.
The nominative goes with τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, not with Christ: the Spirit judges because he is God and Creator.

choices.term: κρινεῖ τα πεινῷ κρίσιν ... ἐλέγξει τοὺς ὑπερηφάνους καὶ ἐξελεῖται τοὺς ταπεινούς
choices.english: he will give judgment to the lowly, and convict the proud, and rescue the lowly of the earth
choices.why: τα πεινῷ is a line-break split of ταπεινῷ. Didymus' text of Isaiah 11:4 differs from the common Septuagint (ἐλέγξει τοὺς ταπεινοὺς τῆς γῆς); his wording is translated.

choices.term: κατὰ τὴν δόξαν ... κατὰ τὴν λαλιάν
choices.english: by appearance ... by what people say
choices.why: δόξα here is outward seeming, λαλιά report or talk.

choices.term: κριτὴν δὲ αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι ἐν τῇ
choices.english: but as judge together with the Holy Spirit, at the…
choices.why: The sentence runs into the next section (δευτέρᾳ παρουσίᾳ ἰδεῖν περιμενόμενον, 'second coming he is awaited, to be seen'); only the words this section holds are translated, ending with '…'.
